title: Type-check coverage gap: e2e/ is outside every tsconfig, so 30 Playwright specs are compiled by nothing
body:
Found while landing #4456 (PR #4470), which closed the **lint** half of this gap for `e2e/`. The **type-check** half is still open, and it is the same defect one gate over.

## Measurement

At `b4d3c2204`, no tsconfig in the repo reaches `e2e/`:

```
$ grep -l '"e2e' tsconfig*.json apps/*/tsconfig*.json packages/*/tsconfig*.json
(no matches)

tsconfig.json                 include: ["packages", "examples", "apps"]
tsconfig.scripts.json         include: ["scripts/**/*.ts"]
tsconfig.vitest-setup.json    include: ["./vitest.setup*.ts", "./vitest.setup*.tsx"]
tsconfig.node.json            (no include/files)
```

`e2e/` is not a workspace package, so `turbo run type-check` structurally cannot reach it either — the same reason given verbatim in `tsconfig.scripts.json`'s header. Playwright transpiles specs without type-checking them, so the 30 `.ts` files under `e2e/` (including `e2e/live/global-setup.ts`, which runs before every live-suite run) have never been compiled by anything.

## Why this is the #3494 shape

#3494 found exactly this for `scripts/`: "not a workspace package, so `turbo run type-check` never reaches it, and `scripts/__tests__` is matched by no `include` in the repo". Its resolution is the ready-made remedy shape here:

- a dedicated `tsconfig.scripts.json` with `include: ["scripts/**/*.ts"]` — a glob, not a file list, so a new file cannot land outside every program again;
- a named root script `type-check:scripts` so it is runnable locally, not CI-only;
- a step in `ci.yml`'s `type-check` job;
- a pin test (`scripts/__tests__/scripts-type-check.test.ts`) holding the config's parse and glob reach in place.

An `e2e` twin of that would be a near-mechanical port. Also worth folding in: `check-type-check-coverage.mjs` has no notion of `e2e/` (it derives from workspace packages), so nothing reports this gap the way `check-lint-coverage.mjs` reports an unlinted package.

## One concrete trap for whoever takes it, already measured

The new `{ cause: e }` in `e2e/live/global-setup.ts` (added by PR #4470 for `preserve-caught-error`) needs **`lib: ES2022` or newer** — `ErrorOptions` does not exist in ES2020, and the root `tsconfig.json` is on `target/lib: ES2020`:

```
$ tsc --lib ES2020,DOM ... e2e/live/global-setup.ts
e2e/live/global-setup.ts(28,7): error TS2554: Expected 0-1 arguments, but got 2.

$ tsc --lib ES2022,DOM ... e2e/live/global-setup.ts
(no such error)
```

So an `e2e` tsconfig must not simply inherit the root's ES2020 lib. `tsconfig.scripts.json` already settled the same question the right way for the same reason — "Node 22 (`engines.node: ">=22"`) is what actually runs these files" — and pins `target/lib: ES2022`. Expect a handful of other standing errors to surface on first compile; that surfacing is the point.

Filed unassigned as a finding while working #4456; not fixed there because it is outside that card's surface (lint wiring plus the 3 error sites).
